Replay. What the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way. WhatsApp replies are written in, not received.
August 2026 · JIVO Oil · 26 working days, 5 Sundays off
51%
of the month’s plan would have been made

21,22,639 L would have come off the lines against a plan of 41,41,400 L across 93 SKUs. The plant actually made 21,19,237 L, so the planner is +0.2% — a modest edge, not a transformation. Storage capped production on 12 of the 26 working days. What held it back was material: a component at zero stopped a planned run on most working days.

The story

  1. 1

    August opened with the godown at 112.3% of its 8,27,000 L working ceiling — only -1,01,314 L of room left. The best production day of the month, 22 Aug, made 1,32,805 L.

  2. 2

    So on 12 of the 26 working days the planner’s decision was the same one: cap production to whatever can ship. Storage stood at 95% on 15 of the 31 days.

  3. 3

    Through the first 14 working days the lines averaged 49% of capacity. On 3 working days across the month — 1, 11 and 18 August — nothing would have been made at all.

  4. 4

    On 18 Aug one big load cleared the floor: 4,60,162 L went out — 4,56,595 L of it on the MART-INTERCOMPANY channel to JIVO MART PVT LTD — which is 23% of everything shipped all month.

  5. 5

    With room to put things, the lines opened up: the 11 working days after that averaged 92% and touched 100% on 3, 4, 5, 6, 20, 21, 22, 24, 25 and 26 August. Then the shortage moved from space to material — 799 planned runs never started for want of an item, and 394 of those came after 18 Aug.

Where the numbers come from

frozen 2026-08-31 · standing on 2026-08-01
opening_fgSAP OITW minus OINM since 2026-08-01, BH-BT+BH-PF, groups 102+115. 461,225 L / 277,774 pcs. Reproduced independently to 0.3 L.
opening_materialsout/aug01-materials-TRUTH.csv — factory app stock-as-of AND SAP rewind; 0 mismatches in 7,858 cells once the day boundary is aligned. SAP OPENING chosen (the factory app returns end-of-day).
standingMeasured per document from BOTH exit doors (/gate-core/sales-dispatch/ + /warehouse/bst/): 467,089 L, 114 docs. 84 of 84 customer docs docked 1 Aug or later.
inboundout/aug01-inbound-TRUTH.csv, credible rows only. Excludes 141,034,848 L of phantom oil (3 POs keyed x1000) and 22.4M units on paper >90 days old (0.0% delivery rate).
linesji.jivo.in line masters. Clear Pack 5L 3,000/hr REFUTED (observed median 831, best 1,068) -> 1,000. Tin Head has NO app config; Aug peak 215/hr. Line clearance 51.3 min median.
efficiencyObserved ~50% of rated when running (median 50.1% per run). Applied — a plan at rated speed is not achievable.
ordersSAP ORDR/RDR1. The factory app has no Oil order book of its own (its Order Processing is a dead OMS mirror, unjoinable, last sync 2026-08-17).
realiseControl Panel, May-Jul 2026 only. No August leakage.
synonymsreference/oil-synonyms.csv. 98.3% of groundnut sits under the peanut alias; RM0000052 olive holds 294,993 L but ALL in BH-OT (Param's) so the godown rule excludes it.
cautionThe factory app is NOT independent of SAP — its own metadata says on-hand is reconstructed from SAP OINM. Agreement is an implementation check, not two measurements.

ONLY 1 August is observed. Every later day is computed. The one thing that arrives daily is that day's POs.

This is a replay, not a record. It shows what the planner would have done in August 2026, standing on each morning with no later data. The factory did not run this way.
Measured: the order book, opening stock, BOMs, line speeds, realise (May–Jul), lead times, storage ceiling, and the people. Assumed: supply arrives exactly on lead time; a 2-day invoice→truck lag; rated line speed rather than the 47% observed. WhatsApp replies are written in by the simulation, not received.
Every number traces to sim/sim-inputs.json.
